# 2009: current events archive

**Source-preservation edition.**

This chronological reference preserves 4,371 Wikipedia event assertions across 365 dates, including topic hierarchy, original citations and pinned revisions. SQLite is authoritative; this UTF-8 Markdown is its readable companion.

Source selection and wording are Wikipedia’s, and are not certified exhaustive, impartial or factually correct. Publication does not imply independent checking of every assertion. Original wording, errors and dated reporting figures remain visible. Editorial accounts are separately labeled and cited.

Database: [2009.sqlite](2009.sqlite). Edition SHA-256: `09057f12543b8d28d2a42db1f79f33a9d3e3e7540bd91ad8d2f985d6bfa94c24`. Publication: `preservation-release-1.1`. Extraction/Markdown profile: `annual-series-1.5`. Date: 2026-10-22.

Original entries without attached citations: 44. Separate editorial evidence: 0; explicitly unverified: 44. Unverified means no full-event verification is established; research may be incomplete or not attempted. An unsuccessful search does not establish that a claim is false. Full-event reviews complete: 0; partial: 0; without a full-event review: 4,371. Partial reviews leave unsupported details explicit.

Exact original daily files, Wikipedia payloads/metadata and prior extraction candidates are embedded losslessly, with hashes, an exact retirement manifest and Git checkpoint. Wikipedia attribution and CC BY-SA obligations remain applicable. Publisher URLs identify evidence; full publisher articles and images are not reproduced.

Template display uses explicit original arguments without calculated conversions, live expansion or inferred links. Unsupported template markup and source reliability tags remain visible. Orphan topics and malformed/unbulleted material are preserved with the handling notes below; no missing child or event is invented.

Commented-out source assertions remain labeled non-event material in the database and handling notes; they are excluded from ordinary event totals.

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Iraq's government announces that all Bremer walls will be removed from Baghdad within forty days.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/8186501.stm>).

**Archived source account.** 11 men drown when a boat sinks on the Nile near Khartoum, Sudan.

Source citations (as archived): [IOL](<https://web.archive.org/web/20060615021453/http://www.int.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1>).

**Archived source account.** Two United States journalists, Laura Ling and Euna Lee, who had been detained by North Korea, return home with former U.S. President Bill Clinton.

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-8"></a>

**Archived source account.** Former Madagascar leader Marc Ravalomanana is hopeful that a relaunch of peace talks between the country's rival factions will bring progress toward a return of political stability.

Source citations (as archived): [IOL](<https://web.archive.org/web/20060615021453/http://www.int.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1>).

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/8186039.stm>).

**Archived source account.** Fourteen people are shot at a women's dance class in LA Fitness gymnasium in Collier Township, Pennsylvania, United States. Three women die, as does the gunman.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/8184697.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-11"></a>

**Archived source account.** Eight people are injured when an Airbus A320 plane catches fire on one of its engines at Paris-Orly Airport. The fire is quickly brought under control.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/rbssIndustryMaterialsUtilitiesNews/idUSL530698720090805>); [BBC News](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/8185594.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-12"></a>

**Archived source account.** Three more men are charged with plotting a suicide attack on a military base in Australia.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC News](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/8184683.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-13"></a>

**Archived source account.** Ireland's Health Service Executive threatens several pharmacies with High Court injunctions if they do not adhere with their contracts to dispense drugs.

Source citations (as archived): [The Irish Times](<http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/breaking/2009/0805/breaking30.htm>); [RTÉ](<http://www.rte.ie/news/2009/0805/pharmacy.html>).

**Archived source account.** Part-nationalised UK lender Lloyds Banking Group reports pre-tax losses of £4 billion for the first half of this year.

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-16"></a>

**Archived source account.** Police fire teargas at protesters rallying in support of Lubna al-Hussein, the Sudanese woman facing 40 lashes for wearing trousers in public.

**Archived source account.** Austrian police probe the shooting of two adolescents who allegedly broke into a supermarket and died by police.

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-21"></a>

**Archived source account.** An anthem sung by FC Schalke 04's fans draws Islamic protests because of its reference to the Prophet Muhammad.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/8185209.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-22"></a>

**Archived source account.** Romanians who fled Belfast following racist attacks return to Northern Ireland.

<a id="event-2009-08-05-0-23"></a>

**Archived source account.** Belgian Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck is under fire after three men with criminal records escape from a courthouse in Brussls. The escape follows the helicopter breakout of three inmates, including one of Belgium's most dangerous criminals, and the ladder breakout of six more convicts all in the space of twelve days.

Source citations (as archived): [Deutsche Welle](<http://www.dw-world.de/dw/article/0,,4543777,00.html>).

Source citations (as archived): [Sapain Tribune](<https://web.archive.org/web/20120224074022/http://www.saipantribune.com/newsstory.aspx?newsID=92515&amp;cat=1>).

### 2009-08-06

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1076511884](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2009%20August%206&oldid=1076511884>).

#### None

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-1"></a>

Context: 64th anniversary of Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings.

**Archived source account.** Japan calls for a nuclear-weapons-free world as it marks 64 years since Hiroshima was hit in the world's first atomic bomb attack.

Source citations (as archived): [RTÉ](<http://www.rte.ie/news/2009/0806/hiroshima.html>); [The Daily Telegraph](<http://blogs.telegraph.co.uk/culture/kateday/100002171/hiroshima-remembering-and-rebuilding/>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-2"></a>

Context: 64th anniversary of Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings.

**Archived source account.** Up to 50,000 people, including officials and visitors from countries around the world, attend a memorial service in the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park built directly below the point where the bomb exploded.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://english.aljazeera.net/news/asia-pacific/2009/08/2009865311526368.html>); [Xinhua](<http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2009-08/06/content_11833234.htm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-3"></a>

Context: 64th anniversary of Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings.

**Archived source account.** Speaking at the ceremony, Mayor of Hiroshima Tadatoshi Akiba supports a call by United States President Barack Obama for the abolition of nuclear weapons.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2009/aug/06/hiroshima-mayor-nuclear-weapons-abolition>); [The Jerusalem Post](<http://www.jpost.com/servlet/Satellite?cid=1249418533509&amp;pagename=JPost%2FJPArticle%2FShowFull>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-4"></a>

Context: 64th anniversary of Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings.

**Archived source account.** The Japanese Government agrees to set up a compensation fund for 300 survivors of the atomic bombings.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC](<http://www.abc.net.au/news/stories/2009/08/06/2648277.htm?section=justin>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-5"></a>

Context: 64th anniversary of Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings.

**Archived source account.** A poll finds 61% of Americans believe their country was correct to drop the atomic bomb on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters India](<http://in.reuters.com/article/worldNews/idINIndia-41560620090805>); [Brisbane Times](<http://news.brisbanetimes.com.au/breaking-news-world/majority-in-us-back-hiroshima-bombing-20090805-e8w8.html>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** Supporters of Iran's opposition leader, Mir-Hossein Mousavi, battle riot police as they hoot horns and take to the streets of Tehran shouting "Death to the dictator".

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/8188830.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** An Indian court sentences to death three people for carrying out bombings that killed more than 50 people in Mumbai in 2003.

Source citations (as archived): [Al Jazeera](<http://english.aljazeera.net/news/asia/2009/08/200986125059910637.html>); [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/8186871.stm>); [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2009/08/07/world/asia/07mumbai.html?_r=1&amp;partner=MOREOVERNEWS&amp;ei=5040>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-8"></a>

**Archived source account.** Malagasy crisis talks resume between interim leader Andry Rajoelina, ousted president Marc Ravalomanana and former presidents Didier Ratsiraka and Albert Zafy in Maputo, Mozambique.

Source citations (as archived): [IOL](<http://www.int.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1&amp;click_id=68&amp;art_id=nw20090806114445868C933057>).

**Archived source account.** New Zealand’s Prime Minister John Key says he believes Fiji’s self-appointed Prime Minister Commodore Frank Bainimarama has given up on the Pacific Islands Forum.

Source citations (as archived): [RNZI](<http://www.rnzi.com/pages/news.php?op=read&amp;id=48238>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-10"></a>

**Archived source account.** Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia express concerns whilst Peru supports a planned accord by Colombian President Álvaro Uribe to allow United States troops to use several bases. Venezuela announces trade measures against Colombia.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/8186767.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-11"></a>

**Archived source account.** Brazil returns 1.500 tonnes of syringes, condoms and dirty nappies which were sent from the United Kingdom.

Source citations (as archived): [MercoPress](<http://en.mercopress.com/2009/08/06/hazardous-waste-illegally-sent-to-brazil-returned-to-uk>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-12"></a>

**Archived source account.** Micro-blogging website Twitter is knocked offline by a distributed denial-of-service attack targeted at a Georgian blogger.

Source citations (as archived): [RTÉ](<http://www.rte.ie/news/2009/0806/twitter.html>); [CNN](<http://edition.cnn.com/2009/TECH/08/06/twitter.attack/>); [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/technology/8189162.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-13"></a>

**Archived source account.** South African photographer Neil Hartmann, accused of documenting Namibia's annual seal cull, is detained without charge for nearly seven hours less than a month after the arrest of two journalists.

Source citations (as archived): [IOL](<https://web.archive.org/web/20060615021453/http://www.int.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1>).

**Archived source account.** A company manager claims that a 77-day occupation of a car plant by hundreds of laid-off workers in South Korea has come to an end.

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-15"></a>

**Archived source account.** Japan's first jury trial for more than 60 years ends with a man in his 70s being sentenced to 15 years in prison for murder.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory?id=8264031>); [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/8188447.stm>); [The Guardian](<http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2009/aug/06/japan-jury-trial-murder>); [The Independent](<https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/asia/praise-for-new-japanese-jury-system-1768198.html>); [The New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2009/08/07/world/asia/07japan.html?partner=MOREOVERNEWS&amp;ei=5040>).

**Archived source account.** Iran bans all pilgrimages to Saudi Arabia during the Islamic holy month of Ramadan in an attempt to contain the spread of swine flu.

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-17"></a>

**Archived source account.** Hundreds of panic-stricken people queue at hospitals in Pune, India, to be tested for swine flu following the first death from the disease in that country.

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-18"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Iraqi cabinet agrees a draft law to restrict smoking in public places and ban tobacco advertising.

**Archived source account.** President Jacob Zuma names Sandile Ngcobo as Chief Justice of South Africa.

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-20"></a>

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-21"></a>

**Archived source account.** At least nine people are killed and several inhale fumes after a fire at a retirement home in Melle, Belgium.

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-22"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Presidents of Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, Joseph Kabila and Paul Kagame, pledge to boost economic and security ties after a rare meeting.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/africa/8188715.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-25"></a>

**Archived source account.** At least 34 people are feared dead after their bus plunges into the Indus River in Pakistan.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/8186819.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-08-06-0-26"></a>

**Archived source account.** The Slender-billed Vulture, one of the world's most endangered birds and said to be rarer than the Tiger, is twice successfully bred in Haryana and West Bengal.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/south_asia/8187533.stm>).

#### None

<a id="event-2009-08-10-0-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** In an open letter four South African opposition leaders accuse President Jacob Zuma of abuse of power after his naming of Sandile Ngcobo as Chief Justice. The office of President Jacob Zuma responds by saying there was "nothing unconstitutional" in Zuma's action.

<a id="event-2009-09-23-0-11"></a>

### 2009-09-24

#### Treaty of Lisbon

<a id="event-2009-09-24-0-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Czech President Václav Klaus says he is "adamant" Irish voters will reject the European Union's Treaty of Lisbon when they vote on it again in the country's 2 October referendum, meaning his unwillingness to sign the treaty will be justified.

Source citations (as archived): [Aktualne](<http://aktualne.centrum.cz/czechnews/clanek.phtml?id=648356>).

<a id="event-2009-09-24-0-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Libertas founder Declan Ganley and Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary clash during high-profile radio and television debates on the Treaty of Lisbon as the referendum campaign intensifies.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/thereporters/gavinhewitt/2009/09/lisbon_fiercely_debated.html>); [Irish Independent](<http://www.independent.ie/national-news/oleary-and-ganley-lock-horns-in-bitter-tv-showdown-1896426.html>).

<a id="event-2009-09-24-0-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** The 2009 G-20 Pittsburgh summit commences with two dozen world leaders in attendance.

No attached source citation. This assertion is unverified; see its disclosure and research status above.

### 2009-09-25

#### None

<a id="event-2009-09-25-0-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Photographs of Spanish Prime Minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero and his family are published in the United States and subsequently published on the front pages of newspapers in his home country. A controversy occurs as many Spaniards have never before seen the children of the intensely private Prime Minister.

Source citations (as archived): [The Guardian](<http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2009/sep/25/spain-zapatero-daughters-obama>).

<a id="event-2009-09-25-0-9"></a>

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/8272508.stm>); [The Times](<http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/environment/article6848627.ece>); [UPI](<http://www.upi.com/Science_News/2009/09/25/Palau-to-create-shark-sanctuary/UPI-25501253888487/>).

### 2009-09-26

[Pinned Wikipedia revision 1328372428](<https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Portal%3ACurrent%20events%2F2009%20September%2026&oldid=1328372428>).

#### Second South America-Africa Summit (ASA) on Isla Margarita

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** The second South America-Africa Summit (ASA) begins on Isla Margarita.

Source citations (as archived): [Xinhua](<http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2009-09/27/content_12114739.htm>); [Bloomberg](<https://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=20601086&amp;sid=as7b1b_qZApE>); [Wall Street Journal](<http://online.wsj.com/article/BT-CO-20090925-712414.html>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** 30 African and South American leaders arrive to attend, with 60 countries being represented.

Source citations (as archived): [CCTV](<http://english.cctv.com/program/newshour/20090927/103103.shtml>); [IOL](<https://web.archive.org/web/20060615021453/http://www.int.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** South African President Jacob Zuma says during the opening of the summit that the South-South union between South American and African regions will contribute to the development of both.

Source citations (as archived): [Xinhua](<http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2009-09/27/content_12114951.htm>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-3"></a>

**Archived source account.** Venezuela's President Hugo Chávez says regional governments are to sign an agreement to create a Bank of the South with startup capital of 20 billion US dollars.

Source citations (as archived): [Wales Online](<http://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/latest-world-news/2009/09/27/seven-nations-to-fund-regional-bank-claims-chavez-91466-24791294/>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-4"></a>

**Archived source account.** A regional bank for South America, the Bank of the South, with a $20-billion initial capital is then set up under an agreement signed by seven nations—Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, Paraguay, Uruguay and Venezuela—on the sidelines of the summit. \{\{Dead link\|date=August 2019 \|bot=InternetArchiveBot \|fix-attempted=yes \}\}

Source citations (as archived): [African Press Agency](<http://www.apanews.net/apa.php?page=show_article_eng&amp;id_article=107668>); [MercoPress](<http://en.mercopress.com/2009/09/27/south-american-leaders-sign-agreement-creating-south-bank>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-5"></a>

**Archived source account.** Libyan leader Muammar al-Gaddafi calls for the creation of a military alliance among nations in the South Atlantic region by 2011, calling it "NATO of the South".

Source citations (as archived): [RTTNews](<http://www.rttnews.com/Content/GeneralNews.aspx?Node=B1&amp;Id=1077523>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-6"></a>

**Archived source account.** More than 100 ministers and heads of state attend a United Nations meeting on the global hunger crisis. Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina tables a five-pronged set of recommendations to raise a hunger-free world.

Source citations (as archived): [Xinhua](<http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2009-09/27/content_12115738.htm>); [RTÉ](<http://www.rte.ie/news/2009/0927/powerp.html>); [Bangladesh News](<https://web.archive.org/web/20110722134316/http://bdnews24.com/details.php?id=143572&amp;cid=2>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-7"></a>

**Archived source account.** At least 10 people are dead in Metro Manila after Tropical Storm Ketsana hits the northern Philippines. \{\{Dead link\|date=August 2019 \|bot=InternetArchiveBot \|fix-attempted=yes \}\}

Source citations (as archived): [AFP](<http://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5iRUDyeGrHCZ6Bd9LyEdrne0FN6hA>); [Philippines Inquirer](<https://web.archive.org/web/20090928112747/http://newsinfo.inquirer.net/breakingnews/nation/view/20090926-227047/Floods-submerge-Metro-Manila-areas>); [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/asia-pacific/8276347.stm>); [Philippine Star](<http://www.philstar.com/Article.aspx?articleId=508807&amp;publicationSubCategoryId=63>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-8"></a>

**Archived source account.** Three detainees held by the United States at Guantánamo Bay in Cuba, are sent abroad to two countries. Ireland accepts two detainees of Uzbeki origin in a humanitarian gesture, with Minister for Justice, Equality and Law Reform Dermot Ahern saying Ireland was one of the first countries in Europe to call for the closure of Guantánamo Bay and that the two men would now be given time to rebuild their lives.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/topNews/idUSTRE58P28P20090926>); [RTÉ](<http://www.rte.ie/news/2009/0927/guantanamo.html>); [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/8277140.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-9"></a>

**Archived source account.** Kenyan President Mwai Kibaki writes to President of the United States Barack Obama to express his concern and disappointment over threats it has received from that country concerning a travel ban on Kenyan officials it blames for hindering reforms.

Source citations (as archived): [IOL](<https://web.archive.org/web/20060615021453/http://www.int.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-10"></a>

**Archived source account.** Two car bomb blasts kill at least 12 people in northwestern Pakistan.

Source citations (as archived): [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/featuredCrisis/idUSSP396592>); [Al Jazeera](<http://english.aljazeera.net/news/asia/2009/09/200992625241814252.html>); [Times of India](<http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/news/world/pakistan/14-killed-in-renewed-suicide-attacks-in-Pakistans-NWFP/articleshow/5058770.cms>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-11"></a>

**Archived source account.** Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad rejects U.S. President Barack Obama's accusation about Iran's nuclear program.

Source citations (as archived): [CNN](<http://www.cnn.com/2009/WORLD/meast/09/25/iran.nuclear/index.html>); [AFP](<http://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5i6jtny6rOmiwS39lfjbJ2n6ybwuQ>); [Al Jazeera](<http://english.aljazeera.net/news/asia/2009/09/200992653918859243.html>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-12"></a>

**Archived source account.** Families separated for over 50 years since the Korean War meet at the Kŭmgangsan resort, North Korea.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/asia-pacific/8276063.stm>); [Yonhap](<http://english.yonhapnews.co.kr/northkorea/2009/09/26/38/0401000000AEN20090926002600315F.HTML>); [Associated Press](<http://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5jTg7x7snBEMQtr6aJWU_5ZAPbwkgD9AUV7V00>); [Xinhua](<http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2009-09/26/content_12114092.htm>).

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/americas/8276038.stm>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-14"></a>

**Archived source account.** A second dust storm hits Sydney, Australia.

Source citations (as archived): [ABC News](<http://www.abc.net.au/news/stories/2009/09/26/2697277.htm?section=justin>); [Xinhua](<http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2009-09/26/content_12114515.htm>); [Bloomberg](<https://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=20601080&amp;sid=aJU3acHEACb8>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-15"></a>

**Archived source account.** Pope Benedict XVI arrives for a three day visit to the Czech Republic.

Source citations (as archived): [CTK](<http://www.ceskenoviny.cz/news/zpravy/pope-benedict-xvi-lands-in-prague-greeted-by-klaus/399695&amp;id_seznam=>); [Press TV](<http://www.presstv.ir/detail.aspx?id=107152&amp;sectionid=351020606>); [Associated Press](<http://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5gmMlaMdpDXTlU__cRV4qy0UFcP3gD9AV08RO0>).

<a id="event-2009-09-26-0-16"></a>

**Archived source account.** Twenty-two large banks in Europe may have accumulated credit losses of close to €400 billion for this year and next, according to officials who have seen a draft of conclusions of “stress tests” conducted by European regulators.

Source citations (as archived): [New York Times](<https://www.nytimes.com/2009/09/26/business/global/26banks.html?adxnnl=1&amp;ref=global&amp;adxnnlx=1253987637-4NFJMpFMq8SPjVfKwgQFQw>).

**Archived source account.** Geelong defeats St Kilda in the 2009 AFL Grand Final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

**Archived source account.** The Spanish government formally unveils plans to liberalise the country's abortion law.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/8276984.stm>).

### 2009-10-03

#### Treaty of Lisbon

<a id="event-2009-10-03-0-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Ireland approves the European Union’s Treaty of Lisbon by a margin of 67.1% to 32.9% in a second referendum.

Source citations (as archived): [RTÉ](<http://www.rte.ie/news/2009/1003/eulisbon1.html>); [The Guardian](<http://www.guardian.co.uk/world/2009/oct/03/ireland-votes-yes-lisbon-treaty>); [Al Jazeera](<http://english.aljazeera.net/news/europe/2009/10/2009103155430453835.html#>); [Toronto Star](<https://www.thestar.com/news/world/article/705136>).

<a id="event-2009-10-03-0-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** Czech President Václav Klaus declines to say how he would proceed in ratification of the Lisbon Treaty after the second referendum is approved by Irish voters.

Source citations (as archived): [The Irish Times](<http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/breaking/2009/1003/breaking6.htm>).

<a id="event-2009-10-03-0-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** The 19th anniversary of the reunification of Germany is marked by a special four-day puppet show in Berlin.

Source citations (as archived): [BBC](<http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/8288375.stm?ls>); [Xinhua](<http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2009-10/04/content_12179093.htm>); [Jamaica Gleaner](<http://www.jamaica-gleaner.com/gleaner/20091003/life/life6.html#>); [Reuters](<https://www.reuters.com/article/yourView/idUS6da7e3f6fc9a1f9c0207d567df1df10420091002>).

#### Presidency of the European Council

<a id="event-2009-10-03-1-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Tony Blair's former chief-of-staff, Jonathan Powell, has been touring European capital cities, including Brussels, Paris and Prague, in an undercover move to make him the first President of the European Council. Blair is supported by French President Nicolas Sarkozy and German Chancellor Angela Merkel.

Source citations (as archived): [The Times](<http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/europe/article6859525.ece#>); [The New Zealand Herald](<http://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/news/article.cfm?c_id=2&amp;objectid=10601055>).

<a id="event-2009-10-03-1-1"></a>

**Archived source account.** William Hague says Blair as EU president would be the worst option for Britain, saying "most people would be extremely annoyed" and that his appointment would "underline the lack of accountability and democracy that is our objection to the Lisbon treaty".

Source citations (as archived): [The Times](<http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/politics/article6859431.ece>).

<a id="event-2009-10-03-1-2"></a>

**Archived source account.** Typhoon Parma hits the Philippines, with early reports indicating at least four deaths as trees are uprooted and roofs torn off houses.

<a id="event-2009-10-15-0-0"></a>

Context: Floods in Great Britain and Ireland:.

**Archived source account.** The Irish Defence Forces are deployed to assist civil authorities after widespread flooding hits the west and south of Ireland after the heaviest rainfall in over thirty years falls in one night. The worst affected areas are Cork and Galway, where there is widespread disruption to public transport and services and several major roads are closed. Lectures at University College Cork are cancelled as the university is submerged.

Source citations (as archived): [RTÉ](<http://www.rte.ie/news/2009/1120/weather.html>); [The Irish Times](<http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/breaking/2009/1120/breaking3.htm>); [Ireland Online](<https://web.archive.org/web/20091123065748/http://breakingnews.iol.ie/news/ireland/university-lectures-suspended-as-floods-hit-ucc-435103.html>).

**Archived source account.** Cumbria, England: A high volume of people, including one policeman, are declared missing, more than 200 people are rescued in Cockermouth and a bridge collapses in Workington during floods. The body of a policeman is later recovered.

### 2009-11-25

#### None

<a id="event-2009-11-25-0-0"></a>

**Archived source account.** Irish floods: Water levels rise between Gort and Kinvara, the main Galway-Limerick road is partially impassable, water levels in Athlone reach 50cm over the highest level on record, Waterways Ireland describes water levels on the River Shannon as "unmanageable" and says one third of Ireland's annual rain has so far fallen during November alone.

<a id="event-2009-11-25-0-2"></a>

Gaston returns to power just nine months after leaving office. This is the eleventh new government in five years.

### 2009-11-26

#### None

<a id="event-2009-11-26-0-0"></a>

<a id="event-2009-11-26-0-1"></a>

<a id="event-2009-11-26-0-2"></a>
